item.title: Apennine Mobilities and Hidden Territoriality. The Case of the Agnone-Pescolanciano Railway Line
item.description: In some areas of the Apennines, the mobility is often described and perceived as difficult, slow and often inadequate. However, in the contemporary landscape, signs of various past forms of mobility (sheep tracks, mule tracks, railway networks, etc.) are still visible. But how does the mobility of the past and the present can dialogue today? And what relations can they generate in territory? item.title: Slow Mobility and Big Data: Exploring the Nexus Between Urban Mobility and Heritage Through GeoAI
item.description: Starting from the new mobility paradigm (Sheller, Urry, 2006), this work explores the use of spatial big data in the field of urban mobility and their connection with cultural and natural heritage at the local scale. The focus is on the nexus between slow mobility and heritage in Pisa (Italy) at the intra-urban scale, employing GeoAI and big data analysis techniques. item.title: Mobility, Tourism and Sustainability: The Case of the “Slow” Motorcycling
item.description: In the context of slow mobility, among the forms of tourism overlooked is motorcycle tourism, often described as a form of short excursions. On the contrary, some motorcyclists who use less powerful and less polluting vehicles organize themselves into small communities (clubs) to enjoy specific landscapes and visit small villages. item.title: Slow Mobilities as a Medium for Re-Semantise the Landscape Heritage: The Case of The Aqueduct Cycle Route in Puglia
item.description: Slow mobility can be considered a medium through which to preserve elements of the landscape identity and to promote new configurations of spaces and places. item.title: Negotiating between Slow Mobility and Heritagisation: Multi-Stakeholder Perceptions, Uses and Perspective Views over Heritage Landscape
item.description: This paper analyses the perceptions, current uses, and perspective views of a peculiar heritage landscape: a linear walkable and cyclable elevated riverbank. Walking and cycling trails are slow-mobility infrastructures that connect different heritage landscapes at local, regional, and transnational levels. item.title: Who will remain? Population Decline in Romania
item.description: Romania was among the last countries to join the European Union in 2007. This event accelerated the ongoing demographic changes in the country triggered by the fall of the communist regime. During the past three decades, intense migration outflows and declining fertility led to a significant reduction in the population, from 22.8 million in 1992 to 19.1 million in 2021, according to census data. item.title: Population Ageing in Italian Municipalities
item.description: In Italy, population ageing is a rapidly growing phenomenon, particularly evident at the municipal level. This study analyzes the trend of population ageing in Italian municipalities from January 1, 2002, to January 1, 2023, considering the geographical characteristics of the municipalities, such as the degree of urbanization and altitude, and the geographical distribution. item.title: The Intensity and Velocity of Ageing Process in Italy at Local Scale: an Empirical Investigation
item.description: The paper proposes an empirical investigation about the spatial dimension of two indicators related to the ageing process: the share of elderly population at the beginning of 2022 and the change (percentage points) in the share of elderly from 2002 to 2022. item.title: Depopulation and Population Ageing: A Demographic Vicious Circle
item.description: Since the post-World War II period, demographic dynamics in Italy, such as increased survival rates, decreased fertility, emigration from certain areas, and an increase in immigration, have quietly and gradually led to changes in the population structure and its territorial distribution: aging and depopulation. item.title: Untapped Potential: Gender and Regional Disparities in Working Life Expectancy and its Trends in Italy
item.description: As societies globally cope with the challenges of an aging population, pension systems face increasing strain. Italy, one of Europe’s largest economies and oldest populations, provides a compelling case for examining the complex interplay between gender and regional disparities in the context of extended working lives. item.title: Demographic Ageing: Challenges and Opportunities. The Case of The Crater Area
item.description: In recent decades, we have witnessed a significant and ongoing shift towards an ageing population, which may pose challenges to economic and social systems.
